clue.text: Set fire to Parliament? Here's a warning of the main dangers

definitions.text: Here's a warning of the main dangers

parts.note: to light something is to set fire to it
the House is a chamber of Parliament, as in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Someone muses on burning down Parliament, then offers a warning of the main dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites arson; in fact it marks a plain charade, and the definition is the whole second sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal tower with a lamp warns shipping of rocks and hazards at sea, the 'main' being the ocean.

clue.text: Reclined in thin shirt

parts.note: lean means thin
a tee or T-shirt gives T

explanation.surface: Someone lounged about in a thin shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is a past tense meaning rested at an angle or lay back.

clue.text: Master, for example, has Howard's End divided into sections

parts.note: a Master of Arts is one kind of degree holder

indicators.note: End is read as the last letter of the name Howard

explanation.surface: A master's student has the novel Howards End split into chapters.
explanation.walkthrough: Howards End is E. M. Forster's novel; here 'Howard's End' is the final letter of Howard, D.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduated means marked off in stages, as on a measuring jug.

clue.text: Protection for hand on shrouds is a form of cheating

parts.note: a thimble protects the finger when sewing
shrouds are the ropes supporting a mast, part of a ship's rigging

explanation.surface: Wearing a hand guard on burial cloths is a kind of dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrouds are not burial cloths but a ship's mast ropes. The answer is the three-cup shell game swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: The swindle where a pea is hidden under one of three cups is a trick to fleece gamblers.

clue.text: Talk about exercises to perform

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for talk surrounds the exercises

parts.note: to orate is to talk at length
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Talking about workouts before performing.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or work, to carry out a task.

clue.text: The lady will get a bill for varnish

parts.note: she'll is the contraction for she will
a/c is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A woman will be charged for her varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin made from insect secretions used as a lacquer or polish.

clue.text: Time one left a voluptuous woman

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the letter standing for one goes away from the word

parts.note: a houri is a beautiful maiden of the Islamic paradise, hence any voluptuous woman
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A moment when someone walked out on a seductive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one left' reads as a person leaving; it is the I dropped from HOURI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty minutes is a unit of time.

clue.text: "Cheered with the grateful smell old — smiles" (Milton)

definitions.text: "Cheered with the grateful smell old — smiles" (Milton)

parts.words: "Cheered with the grateful smell old — smiles" (Milton)
parts.note: a quotation from Paradise Lost, Book IV, with one word missing that the solver fills in

explanation.definitionFit: Milton personifies the sea as smiling when perfumed winds blow off the shore of Paradise.

clue.text: Turned up in store Sure is strange!

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of the two words are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at something odd turning up in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges STORESURE. 'Turned up' is the definition, as in a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A retroussé nose is one tilted upward at the tip.

clue.text: Counter charges of crime possibly in Rhode Island races

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged crime inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible reordering of the word crime

parts.note: nations are races or peoples

explanation.surface: Cross-accusations of possible crime among Rhode Island's ethnic groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CRIME into ECRIM, and 'in' places it inside RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Recriminations are accusations made in return against an accuser.

clue.text: Girl takes food — such greed

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A girl helps herself to food, and such greed is noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an excessive desire for wealth, a synonym of greed.

clue.text: A means of heating sulphur, say

definitions.meaning: the electric coil in a kettle or heater
sulphur is one of the chemical substances in the periodic table

explanation.surface: A heating method involving sulphur, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The heating coil in an appliance and a basic chemical substance both share this name.

clue.text: A handy kind of sketch

parts.note: handy puns on the hand: a small rough sketch is named after a part of the finger

explanation.definitionFit: A small quick drawing is called by the name of the hard plate on the end of the digit.

clue.text: Just the man to perform a piece of music

parts.note: Ron is a man's name
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Someone is just the right man to play a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form with a recurring main theme, often a sonata's final movement.

clue.text: One who has 2 with an article to clean in water

parts.note: 2 down's answer describes someone who has completed a degree, so a BA, Bachelor of Arts
the definite article is THE

explanation.surface: A university leaver, with an article, washes in water.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' is a cross-reference to the answer of 2 down: a person who has done that is a BA.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash or immerse oneself in water.

clue.text: It's fast going downhill, this man's town!

parts.note: Bob's, belonging to a man called Bob
Leigh is a town in Lancashire, and Leigh-on-Sea one in Essex

explanation.surface: A man boasts that his home town is going downhill fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going downhill' suggests decline, but it is the literal descent of a winter sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing sled hurtles down an icy track at high speed.

clue.text: Surround quarters — where they are to be found

parts.note: east and north are two of the four quarters, or cardinal points, abbreviated E and N

parts.words: where they are to be found
parts.note: the cardinal points are marked on a compass

explanation.surface: Surround the quarters, wherever they may be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'quarters' look like lodgings; they are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to encircle or enclose something.

clue.text: A bishop with an unfinished mission church has a mental lapse

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the mission word is cut off

parts.note: an errand is a mission
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman on an incomplete church mission suffers a brainstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrance is a deviation from the normal course, here a straying of the mind.

clue.text: Game for a drink?

definitions.meaning: a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net
A claret cup, an old wine punch with soda and borage

explanation.surface: A sport played for the sake of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is the less familiar sense: a Victorian claret cup named after the Duke of Beaufort's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the shuttlecock sport and an old claret punch take their name from a country house in Gloucestershire.

clue.text: It's unwise to catch any one of these several sailors

definitions.text: It's unwise to catch any one of these
definitions.meaning: the idiom 'to catch a Tartar' means taking on someone too formidable
tar is a sailor, so a tar and more tars

explanation.surface: Several seamen make dangerous catches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch a Tartar' is an old idiom for tackling someone who proves far too strong for you; the second reading splits the word as TAR TARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce Central Asian warriors gave the idiom; split in two, the word is a run of seafarers.

clue.text: Oriental native moving in his simplicity

indicators.note: moving means the letters of native shift about

parts.note: E for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: A native of the East moving with innocent simplicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges NATIVE into NAIVET, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or a lack of worldly experience.

clue.text: Relative newcomer in England conceals early origins

indicators.note: the origins of words are their opening letters, so the first letter of each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A family newcomer settling in England hides where they first came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' looks like part of the indicator 'early origins'; it is the fifth word supplying a letter, and 'origins' alone signals the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: Prone to be careless with the truth

definitions.meaning: stretched out flat on the ground

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to be loose with the facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone' looks like 'inclined to', but it means lying flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means both stretched out flat and telling untruths.

clue.text: "Not out." umpire is upset to conclude

parts.note: a batter who is not out in cricket is still in

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the umpire word is read upwards

parts.note: a ref, referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: An umpire is upset to reach the verdict 'Not out'.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter not out is 'in'. 'upset' turns REF to FER.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce or draw a conclusion from evidence.

clue.text: Rose tired out, having painted the town red

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rose was worn out after a wild night of painting the town red.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily, the same as having a wild night out.

clue.text: Lived in abode

definitions.meaning: the past tense of abide, to stay or reside

explanation.surface: Lived in a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abode' looks like a noun, a home; it is the past tense of the verb abide.
explanation.definitionFit: Both past tenses describe having resided or stayed in a place.

clue.text: Fashionable admirer encounters reserve from the princess

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be in
a fan is an admirer
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army

explanation.surface: A trendy admirer meets a royal princess's reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king.

clue.text: Make a declaration in Reno unceremoniously

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone makes an announcement in Reno without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into RENO UNCEREMONIOUSLY, where the answer runs across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To enounce is to state or pronounce formally.

clue.text: The love of a woman for a demigod

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning belonging to a woman
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman falls in love with a demigod.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth such figures as Heracles were half-divine champions of superhuman strength.

clue.text: Judgement fools people in a way

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: in puts the word for people inside the abbreviation for a way

parts.note: St is short for Street, a way
men are people

explanation.surface: Fools judge people in their own particular way.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is an evaluation or considered opinion.
